Łuków Old Jewish Cemeter

Jewish Cemetery · Łuków, Poland

Not demolished. This record contains a contradiction worth flagging: it is categorized as demolished and overbuilt, yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Łuków's Jewish community is documented from at least the second half of the 15th century, and a 1607 chronicle confirms an organized kehilla already existed by then. After a 1659 fire destroyed the town, the king's rebuilding permit explicitly protected the community's continued use of its 'old' cemetery, implying the site was already well established. This cemetery was used until 1864, when a new cemetery opened; it was destroyed during WWII, its stones used for construction, and by 1954 a hospital complex had been built on the site — no traces remain today, and no tombstones from before 1864 have been found.
